summary: Three full-length passages (825, 859, 867 words) with rising difficulty and a varied IELTS question set; passage 3 on food-storing birds is a good C1 science text. All keys are correct. The Y/N/NG set in passage 3 was slightly out of passage order and has been re-ordered.
strengths: Matching headings has two spare headings and paraphrased headings ("A faster way to grow the slowest corals" for "the reef's marathon runners").
Passage 3 MCQs need inference (Q29: digging where seeds were removed means smell is not the guide).
Sentence endings include a direct trap (C "grows smaller during the autumn months", the opposite of the passage).

issues.problem: Y/N/NG order: Q35 (the scrub-jay experiment, paragraph 4) comes after Q33 and Q34 (paragraph 5).
issues.change: Re-ordered in mock5-reading.js (numbers and types kept): Q33 is now the scrub-jay item (YES), Q34 the laboratory item (NO), Q35 the primates item (NOT GIVEN); explanation, evidence and paraphrase pair moved with each statement in mock-vocab-A.json. Q32-36 now follow passage order.

issues.problem: "superior to that of any mammal" vs the passage "rival those of primates": NOT GIVEN is the right key, but "rival" (are equal to) could be argued to contradict "superior", so a few students may defend NO.
issues.change: Make the statement clearly unaddressed, e.g. "The nutcracker's memory is better than that of any other bird."

issues.problem: The mass spawning is tested twice (heading H for paragraph D and Q26).
issues.change: Change Q26 to another detail, e.g. "What is breeding from corals that survived bleaching called?" (assisted evolution).
